findings.claim_in_model: "First, a declared index the call's own context carries (the contract, the grain of the document) does not move a row out of \"at one call\"; a declared index that is an attribution about the system making the claim (the boundary, the continuity) does, because a system cannot declare those of itself without the circularity the theory forbids."
findings.finding: Builder C asks the judge to press here first, and the rider does not hold. (i) File 11 draws no line between the four indices: "Grain ℓ, boundary β, continuity Ω, and the contract C are declared indices" treats them alike, and the "Declared inputs" paragraph lists the scope of a contract beside the boundary and continuity — so by the record column's own definition ("a declared input from outside") the contract should move a row too. (ii) The rider's stated reason is not in file 11: the circularity Part XIV forbids is "an ownership and a capability justified only by each other", not a system declaring its own boundary; Part XII says the boundary is declared before the attribution, not that the system may not declare it. (iii) The rider's holder is two failing swaps, one of which fails only because "the table does no work" — a usefulness argument, not a holder. A third swap builder C did not run, "an index declared by anyone outside the system moves the row", is killed by neither and moves eight of the twenty-one rows ((O), (Q), contract, (K), (E), (S)(B)(D), (R), (K1)) into the record column. The rider carries those eight rows.
findings.evidence: file 11 Part XIV: "**Indices, not primitives.** Grain \\(\\ell\\), boundary \\(\\beta\\), continuity \\(\\Omega\\), and the contract \\(C\\) are declared indices. Every claim is relative to them; none is a predicate that could be true or false." file 11 Part XIV: "**Declared inputs.** Besides the two primitives, some claims take stated inputs that the semantics records and does not supply: the obligations \\(O\\) and \\(P\\) of a repair, with the occasions each covers (Part XI); the scope of a contract and what makes a restriction appropriate (Part III); the system boundary and continuity of an attribution (Part XII)." file 11 Part XIV: "The order is well founded: a representation justified only by its own construction, or an ownership and a capability justified only by each other, has not supplied its place in it..." W7 C11 Holder: "The two failing swaps: with \"any declared index moves the row\", every row lands in one column and the table does no work; with \"no declared index moves a row\", Deploy, Build, (N) and Can land at one call against \"Ownership is grounded in the processes and resources the boundary includes...\"" W7 §3, after the table: "**Builder C's strongest attack on its own table** ... A judge is asked to press there first."
findings.mark: held if — held if the line between the two kinds of declared index is the theory's; file 11 draws none and groups the contract with the boundary
findings.what_would_show_wrong: A sentence of file 11 distinguishing an index the context carries from an index that is an attribution about the system, or forbidding a system to declare its own boundary. I read Parts XII, XIII and XIV in full and Part X's Ownership passage; the two sentences I found group the four indices together and list the contract's scope with the boundary.

findings.where: Part A7, second sentence, read against part A3
findings.claim_in_model: "Where two arms emit differently under the same inputs, they are different organizations at this grain."
findings.finding: A3 says one organization may emit differently on one context, so an emission difference does not by itself show two organizations; A7's sentence carries no such qualification and W7 names no pull between the two. The counts are safe, because P4.1 measures against an arm-(a)-to-arm-(a) baseline and A3 is the stated reason that baseline exists; the sentence is not. This is the pull that decides how every arm difference in phase 4 is read, and the model has no pairs-that-pull section in which it could be named.

W7 A3 holder: "\"Several solutions remain several.\" (Part II, 10 and 11)". file 11 Part II: "Values of ports may be paths, functions, fields, proofs or histories. Cyclic constraints are admitted. Several solutions remain several." W3 P4.1: "the baseline is the number of documents on which any two of the three repeats of arm (a) disagree". W7 has no section naming pairs that pull; all three builders wrote one in their returns (builder_A "Pairs that pull", builder_B "**Pairs that pull.** Three.", builder_C "**Pull.**").

findings.forced_edit: A7's second sentence reads "...emit differently under the same inputs, beyond the run-to-run spread A3 names, they are different organizations at this grain", and W7 carries the three builders' pull lists.

findings.where: Part A2 and the word-list row "a port", read against parts A4 and B10
findings.claim_in_model: A2: "A passage that no admitted edit reaches is not a port of this account." Word list: "A passage of the context or the emission that some admitted edit reaches; a passage no edit reaches is not a port."
findings.finding: The criterion is used in two senses that cannot both hold. A4 needs "reaches" to mean "sets", so that passages the caller cannot set fall into the boundary conditions — yet A4 also says those passages vary with the arm, so a context edit reaches them. B10 needs the emission passages to be ports a component assigns, yet A2's admitted edits ("change a passage, withhold one, add one") set no emission passage, so under the "sets" reading the emission has no ports and B10's harness replaces nothing. File 11 keeps the two apart: an input is a port an edit sets; an output is a port a component determines.
findings.evidence: file 11 Part II, Roles are derived: "A port \\(v\\) is an **input** under \\(A\\) when \\(A\\) contains an edit that sets \\(v\\) directly. A port is an **output** of component \\(j\\) when its value is determined by \\(L_j\\) given the other ports of \\(V_j\\) across \\(B\\)." W7 A4: "they are in the context and so are in the account's boundary conditions; they are not ports of this contract, because no admitted edit of it sets them. In the reader phase 4 uses they vary with the arm..." W7 B10: "A harness that writes tokens into the emission, or fixes its shape ... sets ports that the organization's own components assign." W7 A2: "whose admitted edits are change a passage, withhold one, add one."
findings.mark: loose — the criterion can be replaced by Part II's own two-clause rule, and should be
findings.what_would_show_wrong: A sentence of file 11 collapsing input and output ports into "ports an edit reaches". Part II states them as two separate clauses.
findings.forced_edit: A2 and the word-list row restate the criterion as Part II states it — input ports are the ones an edit sets, output ports the ones a component determines — and A4's exclusion reads "not an *input* port".

verdict:
**1. The question, frozen.** What is explained: which of the theory's objects an agent built on a large language model instantiates at one call, which across calls, which only with a record or a harness, and which never, so that the skills the workflow needs and the boundaries between them can be drawn from it (W7 §1, W3 §1). Range: agents of the kinds this record has run, at the declared grain of text. What is asked: mixed, and the mixture is stated — rule-status for A1-A4, C2, C5-C10 and most of the table; production for A5 and B10; identification for A7 and B3; blocked for the three \"never\" rows.
